data.title: Drawer
data.tagline: Slide in a side panel without leaving the current page
data.description: A drawer keeps the current page visible while showing details, filters, navigation, or a short editing task from the side. Make the boundary and close behavior clear. If the content needs a lot of space or has its own navigation, use a full page.

use: A short edit that benefits from page context
avoid: Use a narrow drawer for dense, complex content
Let it cover essential context without a reason
Hide how to close or return

lessonPractice.title: From an order list, someone edits a full shipping address while keeping the order visible, then returns to the same position. What fits?

options.label: Open a closable editing drawer from the right and keep the list behind it
options.feedback: A drawer has room for the form while preserving order context and the list position after closing.

options.label: Open a fixed-size confirmation modal in the center
options.feedback: A confirmation modal suits a short decision; a full address form becomes cramped and hides more context.

options.label: Navigate to an address page and return to the top after saving
options.feedback: A separate page can edit the address, but it loses the requested order context and list position.

data.agentPrompt: Open a shipping-address editor in a right drawer while preserving the order and scroll position behind it. Add a title, close control, and save feedback, then test focus, return position, and mobile layout.
